properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-28, marked "a follow-on task as it is the least important for now": "transform reflow2 repo main README.md into a very minimalist document or replace with index.html and make github.io pages the documentation. Also, I'd like to largely replace the docs with a few clean .html files that the index.html points to ... In essence, I'd like to really clean up the git repo. If we are required to have a README.md, then make it minimal. If not, just have an index.html that points to something like: sligara7.github.io/reflow2 where people can see the documentation. Even then, I'd like to keep this clean. If we can make the reflow2 pages follow a similar layout as: https://flo2.io/, that would be great."

WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY HOLDS, read before this was written:
· req:reflow2-has-a-public-page-anyone-can-read (PROPOSED, his words of 2026-08-14): a live page on GitHub Pages. It already flags the ROOT placement as the part to re-examine, because the root is a Rust workspace. Pages can serve from /docs or from an Actions deploy instead.
· dec:idea-what-is-on-reflow2s-public-page (ACCEPTED 2026-08-14): the public page carries ONLY renderings the agent generates from reflow2's own graph. His words then: "I'd like to only use renderings of systems engineering views the agent generates from graph content of reflow2 itself." Its own text: "A page whose entire claim is 'this came from the graph' is FALSIFIED by one hand-written fact." Hand-written HTML documentation pages would therefore reopen that decision. That is Anthony's call, and it is put to him rather than offered here as a live option.
· COORD.md states the repo's rule for documents: "a document holds what is addressed to someone without the tool; the graph holds what the tool can compute."
· Measured: docs/ holds 63 entries. 25 docs files are registered Artifacts, several of which DOCUMENT accepted requirements (docs/vision.md among them, registered today). tools/render_views.py already renders viewpoints from the graph.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) A MINIMAL README: what reflow2 is in a paragraph, how to install it, and a link to the site. GitHub shows a README on the repository page, and an index.html at the root is NOT rendered there, so some README is the only front door a visitor to github.com/sligara7/reflow2 sees.
(b) NO README: an index.html (served by Pages) as the only front door. The repository page then shows a bare file list.
(c) THE SITE IS GENERATED FROM THE GRAPH: the few clean pages (what it is, install, how it works, the loop) are renderings of the design itself, in flo2.io's layout. This stays inside the accepted "only renderings" decision, and the prose docs retire into the graph they already duplicate.
(d) THE SITE IS HAND-WRITTEN: a few clean HTML pages. It is simpler to write, and it needs the accepted 2026-08-14 decision reopened.
(e) SERVE FROM WHERE: /docs on main, a gh-pages branch, or an Actions deploy. Actions keeps generated HTML out of the source tree entirely.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
· Docs are wired in. Registered artifacts DOCUMENT accepted requirements; check_doc_versions checks version claims in the docs; skill_lint reads AGENTS.md; CHANGELOG and README link into docs/. Retiring them is a design act (the artifacts retire on the record), not only a git rm.
· Generated pages (c) are the larger build, and a site generator is a new moving part. Hand-written pages (d) are smaller and drift, which is the failure the accepted decision was written against.
· A public site is outward-facing and indexed once published.
· FOR IT: 63 docs entries (20 of them upgrade notes) is a lot for a newcomer. A few pages in a clean layout serve the core identity, a person with no systems-engineering background, better than a folder of engineering notes.

SIZE, AS INFORMATION: (a) is small. (e) is small. (c) is medium to large. (d) is medium, plus reopening a decision.
